hints: Treat the modulus piecewise, changing its form at \(x=3\).
For \(x<3\), use \(|x-3|=3-x\); for \(x\ge3\), use \(|x-3|=x-3\), and solve the strict inequality in each case.
Retain only solutions belonging to their assumed case, then combine them with an open boundary because the original inequality is strict.
walkthrough:
Observe that the right-hand side $2|x - 3| \ge 0$ for all real $x$. Therefore, any real solution must satisfy:
$$2 - 5x > 0 \implies 5x < 2 \implies x < \dfrac{2}{5} = 0.4$$

Since $x < 0.4 < 3$, the expression inside the modulus is strictly negative, so $|x - 3| = -(x - 3) = 3 - x$:
$$2|x - 3| = 2(3 - x) = 6 - 2x$$

Substitute this definition into the inequality for $x < 3$:
$$2 - 5x > 6 - 2x$$

Alternatively, determine the critical value algebraically by squaring both sides under the domain condition $x < \dfrac{2}{5}$:
$$(2 - 5x)^2 > 4(x - 3)^2$$
$$4 - 20x + 25x^2 > 4(x^2 - 6x + 9) = 4x^2 - 24x + 36$$
$$21x^2 + 4x - 32 > 0$$
$$(3x + 4)(7x - 8) > 0$$
The critical values are $x = -\dfrac{4}{3}$ and $x = \dfrac{8}{7}$. Since $x < \dfrac{2}{5}$, the valid region is strictly $x < -\dfrac{4}{3}$.

ai_rubric.Solving Inequalities: Makes a sketch of $y=2|x-3|$ and the line $y=2-5x$. Finds the $x$-coordinate of intersection with $y=2-5x$. The final result is $x<-\frac43$.
